A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same compression framework, renamed from Taco-SVD to GRASP. All 14 pages of v1 and 16 pages of v2, including equations, figures, tables, and appendices, support comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original LLaMA/Mistral compression experiments, calibration and pruning ablations, post-training results, and hardware measurements.

after.justification: v2 retains original experiments and adds LLaMA-7B, GSM8K, and LongBench results. Some SVD-LLM comparator scores are explicitly attributed to prior work, but original results are clearly present.

M1.justification: Cosine-based layer selection, gradient-weighted singular-value ranking, top-k retention, backward layerwise compression, and optional fine-tuning remain unchanged. RLAL explicitly specifies the language-model loss used with calibration data; the PDFs do not establish a changed computational procedure.

E1.justification: v2 adds GSM8K generation and LongBench evaluation spanning long-context QA, summarization, few-shot learning, synthetic tasks, and code completion, including English and Chinese datasets. C4 perplexity evaluation disappears, although C4 remains in the calibration ablation.

E2.justification: ShortGPT enters the tabulated pruning comparisons, and FWSVD and SVD-LLM join ASVD in dedicated SVD comparisons (v2 Tables 1, 3–4). These methods were previously discussed but lacked these comparisons. LoRA and both LLM-Streamline variants remain; Table 4 identifies its SVD-LLM scores as sourced from prior work.

E3.justification: v2 replaces the LLaMA2-7B compression sweep with LLaMA-7B evaluation extending to 50% compression and specifies five-shot exact-match evaluation for GSM8K. It removes v1 Appendix A.3's conflicting 256-sample calibration statement while retaining 512 samples in the main setup; this reporting revision does not establish that existing experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: The compression-ratio sensitivity analysis changes model, comparator set, and range (v1 Figure 3/Table 7 versus v2 Table 3). Calibration-dataset and sample-count ablations, one-shot versus iterative pruning, and convergence analysis are retained, mostly through relocation and renumbering.

E5.justification: Neither version reports seeds, repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. Benchmark averages and validation-loss curves do not introduce uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: v2 adds extensive SVD, GSM8K, and LongBench result entries while removing C4 scores and the earlier LLaMA2-7B high-compression sweep. Mistral WikiText-2 perplexity changes from 26.42 to 18.42 in Table 1, but compression-ratio and calibration reporting differences prevent treating this as an established same-setting improvement.

T1.justification: v2 Equation 2 adds an explicit mathematical definition of RLAL as next-token negative log-likelihood, whereas v1 leaves the task loss unspecified. The Taylor approximation, singular-value importance formula, and Appendix A.1 derivation otherwise remain unchanged; no new theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: The central objective is redefined from aligning compression with downstream task-specific objectives to preserving general linguistic representations. v2 explicitly distinguishes RLAL from optimization for particular downstream applications and presents the contribution as a hybrid pruning framework. Broad performance and efficiency claims remain.

C2.justification: v2 hypothesizes calibration overfitting to explain the WikiText-2/PTB discrepancy in baseline performance and interprets LongBench results as evidence of recovery through post-training. The self-repair and low-rank-learning explanations largely remain, as do the three stated limitations.

D1.justification: v2 adds a source-code access link in the abstract and explicitly documents the next-token loss. Appendix Table 9 also identifies Mistral-7B-v0.1. The detailed Alpaca hyperparameter table, optimizer, A100 hardware, and compression-cost measurements are retained.

R1.justification: v2 develops three explicit distinctions from conventional SVD compression and adds a descriptive comparison of pruning methods in Appendix Table 7. References add LongBench, GSM8K, and the original LLaMA paper and remove Yaras et al. (2024); the main related-work foundation remains.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, and method motivation are extensively rewritten around GRASP and representation preservation. Related-work subsections are merged, experiments are reorganized into separate comparison sections, discussion is condensed, and appendix organization changes substantially.

P2.justification: Figure 2 is redrawn with separate SVD and layer-removal comparison panels. Main result tables are restructured into model-column summaries, with detailed reasoning scores moved to appendices. New SVD and LongBench tables replace or supplement earlier displays, and cost and pruning-ablation tables move to appendices.

improvement.justification: Expanded baselines, GSM8K/LongBench evaluation, loss specification, and a code link improve coverage and documentation. However, new Table 4 reports LLaMA2 original perplexities of 5.68/5.47, conflicting with Table 1's 5.47/4.88, and its 20% caption accompanies post-training scores also reported near 25% elsewhere. These inconsistencies undermine an important added comparison, leaving the net quality improvement uncertain.
